# Wireless charging pad installation

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Adhere a wireless charging module and run a micro-USB cable from a fused 12-volt plug. [t483]

[Partial] Run a cord through the center console and plug the new adapter's micro USB connector into the existing 12 V socket. [t483]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Gather a wireless charging module and run a micro-USB cable.
2. Locate the fused 12-volt plug in the back of the center console.
3. Connect one end of the micro-USB cable to the charged 12-volt plug.
4. Adhere the wireless charging module to the bottom of the center console tray.
5. Position your phone diagonally on top of the module if necessary for alignment.
6. [Partial] Turn the keyswitch in the vehicle's ignition to the 'on' position.

_Procedure reported by [t483]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-touch-of-modern-wireless-charging.9810/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t483] [Partial]</summary>

1. Run a cord with micro USB on one end and a standard 12 V plug on the other through the center console into the armrest area.
2. [Partial] Plug the new adapter's micro USB connector into the existing 12 V socket.

</details>

## Parts

- [Partial] Extension cord with 12 V plug end: One side is standard 12 V, other is micro USB [t483]
- Qi wireless charging pad: Must have a built-in micro USB input [t483]
- [Partial] Wireless charging module: Triple coil design with micro-USB input [t483]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Run a fused 12-volt plug into the back of the center console to power the unit. [t483]
- Use an extension cord to route the power source conveniently. [t483]
